doc.title: Pete Levin interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001

title: Business card and Levin's many professional identities
summary: Monk Rowe asks what Levin's business card says; Levin explains he is known in different circles as jazz player, pop sideman and classical orchestrator, and that these worlds rarely meet.

story.theme_name: Opening the interview: Monk Rowe's welcome and archive boilerplate
story.community_name: Opening the Hamilton College interview: introductions and boilerplate

blocks.x: My name is Monk Rowe and we are in Danbury, Connecticut. I’m very pleased to have Pete Levin with me today for the Jazz Archive. And I was looking at your resume and so forth, and I’m wondering, if you have a business card, what does it say on it?
Yes. How do you promote yourself?
I do have, just my name and a line drawing of me and a phone number. That’s it. That’s all that’s there.
Because you do so many things. I’m wondering if you have a reputation now as one particular — in your electronic field or as a jazz player or arranger?

I think probably not in one particular field, because I’ve gone into a lot of areas as a sideman and as a writer. It takes a long time — I’ve always been based out of New York. For a long time there was a large segment of people who knew me as a jazz player and never hired me for anything else, like a pop gig of some kind, although I’ve done a lot them with small names and with big names. But the two things never met somehow. And way back in my roots I’m a classically trained French horn player with a masters from Juilliard. Also I’ve got a strong background in classical, and I actually orchestrate the stuff I write for orchestra and large ensembles. But nobody in the jazz world is aware of that, so I’ve got a bunch of different people, depends on who you talk to.
Yeah. I wonder if they’d be surprised to know that you have these other lives actually.

I don’t know if it’s surprised or not, they just don’t — well if somebody in the jazz world is saying well I need somebody who can write for strings, they wouldn’t think to call me, even though I was next to them on the bandstand the night before.
